I've been working this land for fifty years, and my body knows the rhythm of it even when my knees don't cooperate anymore. Quzhou gets dry springs and hot summers — that's why the well matters. My sons are in the city now, so I hire the village machinery cooperative for ploughing and harvest. I can't manage the heavy work alone at my age.

**Wheat (October planting, June harvest):**
I'll plant the whole field — all 16.9 mu — to Jimai 22 or the improved variety the county seed store is selling this season. I've tried the fancy high-input varieties but they need too much care. I'll do rotary tillage after I harvest the maize in autumn, broadcast my compound fertilizer as base, then top-dress with urea at jointing in April. Four irrigations: one soaking before seeding so the seeds germinate well, one in November before the ground freezes to protect the roots, one at jointing in March, one at heading in May. I'll spray fungicide once for rust — that's been bad the last couple of years — and aphicide once before grain fill. That's how I've always done it and I get decent yields.

**Maize (June planting, October harvest):**
Right after I cut the wheat, I direct-seed the maize into the stubble. No need to plough again — saves money and my back. I buy Xianyu 335 hybrid seed from the township store, everyone around here uses it, I know what to expect. I'll fertilize well at planting — one application of compound fertilizer — and topdress heavy with urea at the big bell stage in August when the plant is hungry. Summer rains help but I'll irrigate three times: once at emergence if dry, once at big bell, once at grain filling. Two pesticide sprays — armyworm has been coming earlier lately.
